{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Collaborative Research, Development and Commercialization Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Sanofi)  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, proposed redlines and diligence items

## Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The overall risk allocation is favourable to us: the licence grant, IP ownership and joint-technology construct, assignment and change-of-control mechanics, termination for convenience, audit reciprocity, governing law and the exclusivity/non-solicit/MFN/minimum-commitment position all sit at or above our preferred position, and several provisions (exclusive licence even as to RevMed, RevMed non-compete, post-termination royalties running to us, Sanofi-only self-insurance election) run affirmatively in our favour and are not redlined.

We have identified **two deviations** requiring redlines, both in Article XIV:

1. **No aggregate liability cap (critical).** Section 14.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision. It gives a mutual consequential-damages waiver with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality and IP, but there is no monetary cap of any kind, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited on both sides. That fails the fallback, whose material term is a mutual 12-month cap. Because exposure is symmetric, we propose the minimal fix rather than a wholesale rewrite.
2. **No third-party IP infringement indemnity (high).** RevMed's indemnity at Section 14.1 covers negligence/willful misconduct and breach of reps and obligations, but has no IP limb. IP exposure reaches RevMed only through the knowledge-qualified, Execution-Date-limited rep at 13.2(f), while 13.5 disclaims non-infringement, 10.7 puts the first burden of a third-party licence on us, and our own indemnity at 14.2(a) covers Third Party Claims arising from our exploitation of Products. We propose adding a direct IP limb with customary exclusions.

One rule — **non-compete restrictions binding the Customer** — could not be completed by the automated review and requires manual verification before we clear the Agreement. Separately, several material figures are redacted ([\*\*\*]) in this copy and must be confirmed against the unredacted text before signature.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Intellectual Property Rights (Art. X; §§10.1, 10.2(a), 10.4(b), 10.5, 3.2, 3.4, 6.2) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§§14.5, 14.6) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (§15.2; cf. §§12.2(a)(ii), 12.3) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | License (§§3.1(a), 3.5(a); Art. VII; §12.2(d)) |
| High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§§14.1, 14.2(a), 14.3, 14.5; cf. §§13.2(f), 13.5, 10.7) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§12.2(a)(i), 12.3(c), 12.6; cf. §9.6, §5.6(b)) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | License (§§3.1(a), 3.4, 3.2; §§12.2(b)–(e), 12.3(b), 15.2(a)(ii)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Needs review** (automated review failed) | Not determined |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§12.2(a)(i), 12.2(b)–(e), 12.3(c)) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (§9.9; cf. §9.8, §6.9) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions (§§15.5, 15.6(a), (h), (j)) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Financial Provisions (Art. IX; cf. §3.5(b)) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Manufacturing and Supply (§§7.3, 8.2, 8.3; Art. IX; §5.7) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | General Provisions (Art. XV; Art. IV) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | Term and Termination (§§12.1, 12.2(a)) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | Confidentiality; Publication (§11.6; §§12.3(b)–(e), 12.4) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Representations, Warranties and Covenants; Closing Conditions (§§13.1(c)–(e), 13.2, 13.4, 13.5; §§14.1(b)–(c), 12.6, 7.3) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | Indemnification; Liability; Insurance (§14.6) |

## Walk-Away Items

On the verified findings, **no clause falls into walk-away territory**:

- **Liability (§14.5):** the absence of a cap is symmetric, not one-sided, so it is a deviation to be fixed by redline rather than a walk-away.
- **IP ownership (Art. X):** the joint-ownership construct in §10.1(b) carries an unrestricted right to exploit and license without accounting or consent, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, sublicensable licence outside the US, so it sits at or above our preferred position.
- **Dispute resolution (§15.6(a)):** JAMS-administered, US-domestic arbitration with court support and patent/trademark carve-outs is within tolerance, not foreign-seated arbitration. **Caveat:** the seat is redacted; a foreign seat would convert this to a deviation.
- **Audit (§9.9):** no right of direct or remote access to our systems, so the walk-away scenario is absent.
- **Warranty (§13.5):** the disclaimer is mutual and expressly prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," so it is nowhere near an "AS IS" position.
- **Transition (§11.6):** deletion of our Confidential Information occurs only on request, so there is no risk of unilateral or immediate deletion of our data.
- **Non-compete:** we cannot confirm the absence of a walk-away trigger until the outstanding manual review is completed.

## Next Steps

1. **Issue two redlines to Article XIV:**
   - **§14.5:** insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' payments made by Sanofi and USD 1,000,000; preserve the existing carve-outs (Art. X, Art. XI, §§14.1/14.2), add gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud, and confirm that Sanofi's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. The existing final sentence stays intact so indemnity and confidentiality/IP claims remain uncapped.
   - **§14.1:** add limb (d) covering Third Party Claims of infringement or misappropriation arising from the RevMed Licensed Technology, with customary modification and combination exclusions, and conform the "(a) through (c)" cross-reference in the carve-out.
2. **Complete the non-compete review manually.** The automated pass on restrictions binding us did not conclude; we will re-run this against Articles III, V and XII (noting §12.2(d) is a conditional termination right, not a covenant) before clearing.
3. **Confirm redacted figures against the unredacted execution copy**, specifically: the Sanofi/RevMed/joint allocation sentence in §10.1(a); the §12.2(a)(i) convenience notice periods (target 30–90 days); the §9.9 audit frequency, notice, look-back and underpayment percentages (target no more than once per Calendar Year, at least 30 days' notice, 5% threshold); and the §15.6(a) arbitral seat and arbitrator count (seat must be New York or another accepted US location).
4. **Note for the file, not for negotiation:** the §11.6 destruction-only mechanic (no machine-readable return) and "promptly" rather than a fixed 30-day outside date; the absence of dollar limits and a one-year tail in §14.6; no express bar on RevMed assigning to a Sanofi competitor on its own change of control; and §12.3's cut-off of RevMed's post-termination royalties on a Change of Control of Sanofi, which we will track as termination economics.
5. **Reserve product-quality and GMP warranties** for the Supply Agreement and Quality Agreement to be negotiated under §7.3, which is their correct home."}
